nodes.label: AMPM Platform Decision Brief (24 Oct 2026, updated 25 Oct 2026)
nodes.rationale: Client-facing brief: Part 1 the platform in one picture, Part 2 eight short sections on what AMPM's documents left open and the defaults taken meanwhile, Part 3 the 25 decisions with AMPM's 25 October answers and the points still to confirm; nothing was decided for AMPM and every default is marked so it can be overturned; the full developer package sits behind it.

nodes.label: Journey stage: public website (learn, examples, request a demo)
Journey stage: demo or trial granted by Sales, expires
nodes.rationale: Marked new: mentioned but not defined in AMPM's documents.

nodes.label: Journey stage: subscription (AMPM invites, client pays, hotel discovery opens)
Journey stage: hotel discovery and assistance (search, verified prices, enquiries, visits, proposals)
nodes.rationale: Prices and verification are new: the specification had no price entity.

nodes.label: Journey stage: stays a subscriber (renews or expires, nothing deleted)
nodes.rationale: Marked new: the branch for clients who never hire AMPM for the wedding.

nodes.label: Journey stage: wedding project (functions, budget, vendors, designs, approvals)
Journey stage: guests (private RSVP link per household, rooms, travel)
nodes.rationale: Partly new: the link model and per-person data were undefined.

nodes.label: Journey stage: wedding day (readiness checks, cue sheet, incidents)
Journey stage: closure (checklist, final accounts, feedback, archive)
Brief section 1: getting in and paying
nodes.rationale: Nobody signs up by themselves and AMPM creates every account; missing were how a demo is granted and ends, one-time vs recurring, how account creation fits online payment and what an expired subscriber sees. Default: Sales grants a time-boxed demo from the enquiry record; AMPM creates the account and invites the client, who pays in the portal online or by bank transfer; one-time fee for a fixed period; on expiry saved hotel names and read access remain and nothing is deleted.

nodes.label: Brief section 2: hotels and prices
nodes.rationale: The specification's data model has no place to store a price or availability and previous clients' photos need permission. Default: rate cards by season with line items verified on a date by a named team member and shown as Stale after a set period; availability answered inside each enquiry, not a calendar; every photo and video carries a rights status; hotel data importable from spreadsheets.

nodes.label: Brief section 3: money, how AMPM earns and what the client sees
nodes.rationale: Unknown whether AMPM earns a margin inside prices or a visible fee, whether clients pay milestones in the portal and which hotel services carry a fee. Default: the stricter case, every price has a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost that never leaves the server; clients see estimates, approved amounts, invoices, payments and next milestone; availability checks included in the subscription, other hotel services by agreement.

nodes.label: Brief section 4: the client side, who logs in and who approves
nodes.rationale: In many weddings the parents pay and the couple designs. Default: three client roles per wedding and a separate switch for who may see money; one approval completes a decision; staff may record a phone decision only with a note or document attached and the portal shows it was recorded on their behalf.

nodes.label: Brief section 5: guests, RSVP and privacy
nodes.rationale: Default: guest list loaded first and a private link per household so nobody sees another family and nothing is duplicated; households may add members up to an allowance; meal preference for everyone, allergies optional and seen only by hospitality; identity documents only when a wedding needs them for hotel check-in, never Aadhaar, locked store, deleted thirty days after checkout; guests see a short privacy notice first.

nodes.label: Brief section 6: the wedding day and closure
nodes.rationale: Staff use phones inside ballrooms and lawns with poor signal. Default: cue sheet, readiness checks and arrival lists readable offline with offline updates sent when signal returns; a function cannot go live until every required check is done or a named manager records an exception; closure is a checklist verified against the data; the couple keeps read-only access for twelve months, then the wedding is archived.

nodes.label: Brief section 7: the flowcharts and the specification disagree
nodes.rationale: The client-portal flowchart has no hotel area although hotel discovery is the paid product and its countdown assumes a wedding date; the team-app flowchart has no place for the Hotel or RSVP teams and nothing before a wedding exists. Default: the portal gains a Hotels tab and a subscriber home page; the team app keeps five tabs on phones and the nine specification areas on desktop; questions and change requests are tracked requests rather than live chat; both flowcharts are redrawn box by box.

nodes.label: Brief section 8: technology and operations
nodes.rationale: Open were native app vs website, hosting and recovery, channels, sign-in, size and website editing. Default: a responsive installable website, hosted in an Indian cloud region with copies in a second Indian region and recoverable to within fifteen minutes; email, WhatsApp and SMS; staff sign in with an authenticator code, clients with email and password plus optional phone code, guests through their private link; sized for fifty staff, forty weddings, fifteen hundred guests and five hundred hotels; a simple website editor.

nodes.label: Principle: nobody can self-register; AMPM invites every client and prospect
nodes.rationale: The Why note says so although the specification does not; confirmed by AMPM.

nodes.label: Principle: a subscription grants hotel modules only; wedding modules come only from a service agreement and a project
nodes.rationale: AMPM's critical rule that one service stage never implies the next; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: expiry or cancellation turns access read-only and never deletes records
nodes.rationale: The Why note says so and nothing else defined it; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: a wedding project is created when an agreement for anything beyond hotel help is accepted
nodes.rationale: Follows business steps 5 and 6; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: only a name, the account, tentative dates and a lead are required to create a wedding
nodes.rationale: Rule 2, not everything mandatory; confirmed, and the client also enters couple, contact, dates and locations at activation.

nodes.label: Principle: every price has a client-facing amount and a separate internal cost that never leaves the server
nodes.rationale: Rule 1 and the specification's security note; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: vendor contact details stay internal even after a vendor is selected
nodes.rationale: AMPM's rule that vendor negotiations are private, although some couples will want to call their photographer; confirmed, with AMPM able to share a specific contact in an approved case.

nodes.label: Principle: five to ten vendor options is a guideline, never enforced
nodes.rationale: The acceptance test says so; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: a decision locks the exact version; a revision is a new version with a new approval
nodes.rationale: The acceptance test says so; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: guests are counted one person at a time, grouped into households
nodes.rationale: Children, rooms and meals need per-person counts; confirmed, children included.

nodes.label: Principle: caterer headcounts are frozen when sent while expected counts keep moving
nodes.rationale: Catering contracts guarantee a number; not addressed by AMPM, stands.

nodes.label: Principle: a function cannot go live with a required check unmet unless a named manager records an exception
nodes.rationale: The specification's readiness rule; confirmed, only Eva's authorised personnel may record the exception.

nodes.label: Principle: prices, fees, categories and thresholds are settings the team changes, never code
nodes.rationale: The specification's rule of no hard-coded commercial rules; confirmed.

nodes.label: Principle: the system is built for AMPM alone, not for licensing to other planners
nodes.rationale: The Why note calls it a paid business asset, which could mean either; confirmed.

nodes.label: Part 3 decisions: 25 questions with assumed defaults and AMPM's 25 Oct 2026 answers
nodes.rationale: Ten questions unblock the design sign-off, fifteen can wait for building or later phases; each carries what was assumed and what AMPM decided.

nodes.label: Still to confirm before design sign-off (AMPM's 11 points plus web portal and client-facing amounts)
nodes.rationale: These points are what remains before the screen designs and the data model can be signed off and the schedule and cost estimate drafted.
